outcome.title: Cut involuntary churn from failed card payments
outcome.statement: Ledgerline customers on monthly plans churn when their card payment fails and nobody notices. Today a failed charge sends one email and then the account is suspended after 7 days. We want to recover most of these customers automatically: retry intelligently, tell the customer clearly what happened and how to fix it, and give our support team visibility into who is at risk before the suspension hits.

success_metrics.target: Support can list at-risk accounts without engineering help

expected_questions: retry engine: Stripe Smart Retries vs own schedule

outcome.title: Make `lintr check` usable in CI
outcome.statement: Teams run our Python CLI linter locally but cannot use it in CI because it exits 0 on findings, prints colour codes into logs, and has no machine-readable output. We want CI pipelines to fail on findings above a configurable severity and to publish results as a report CI systems understand.

success_metrics.target: Internal pipelines can gate on lintr
success_metrics.measurement: exit code semantics and SARIF output verified by hidden tests

must_not: No change to existing rule semantics

expected_questions: which report format: SARIF, JUnit XML, or both

outcome.title: Customers can choose how we contact them
outcome.statement: We send email for everything. Enterprise customers are asking for Slack and webhook delivery of alerts, and for per-event-type preferences. Legal has flagged that marketing and transactional messages must be separable for consent reasons. We want a notification preferences capability that lets each account pick channels per event type, with transactional messages always deliverable.

must_not: No change to the existing email templates

expected_questions: which event types count as transactional
